title: BAGMAN MailboxSource
description: An operator-registered mailbox DEFINITION BAGMAN will later monitor for evidence (CD-6 Slice 3, PID §98.4-following, architect scope: 'operator-facing mailbox registry and management foundation only'). A `MailboxSource` is explicitly NOT a BAGMAN company/accounting entity/Xero organisation/ledger/invoice owner — it is a source of evidence, nothing more; `default_entity_id` is only ever an optional DISPLAY hint (never an ownership assertion — mirrors `core.source.Source.governed_entity_hint`'s own doctrine exactly, see `persistence/postgres/models.py`'s own note on that field). This slice creates/edits/enables/disables/retires mailbox definitions only — no provider OAuth/IMAP login, no mail fetch, no sweep scheduler, no evidence creation from email exists anywhere behind this contract yet (see `services/mailbox/mailbox.py`'s own module docstring for the full out-of-scope list). NEVER carries a password/OAuth token/refresh token/client secret/app secret/private key of any kind, anywhere, at any time (no such field exists on this contract, and none may ever be added to it) — see that module's own 'Secret doctrine' section.

mailbox_id.description: Canonical BAGMAN identifier for this mailbox definition row.

display_name.description: Operator-facing label for this mailbox (e.g. 'Matt — Infosecurs'). Free text, never business truth on its own.

email_address.description: The real mailbox address this definition names. Always stored and compared lowercase (normalised by `services/mailbox/mailbox.py`/`persistence/postgres/mailbox_repository.py` before either uniqueness comparison or storage — see those modules' own docstrings for the exact, documented uniqueness rule chosen: GLOBAL uniqueness across every mailbox regardless of provider or lifecycle status). Never itself a secret — an email address is not credential material — but never accompanied anywhere on this contract by a password/token of any kind.

provider_kind.description: The FUTURE adapter family this mailbox definition declares — deliberately an OPEN string field at the CONTRACT layer (never a closed JSON Schema `enum`/`const` naming a specific external provider brand): this repository's own `tests/integration/test_architecture_boundaries.py::test_no_schema_file_hardcodes_a_provider_name_inside_a_structural_constraint` forbids exactly that. `services/mailbox/mailbox.py` separately enforces a CLOSED, Python-level set (`PROVIDER_KINDS`) — mirroring `services.xero.connection.PROVIDERS`'s identical closed-set doctrine one layer down, and `ai.invocation.PROVIDERS` before that. No code anywhere behind this field ever calls out to any provider in this slice — it exists purely so a mailbox definition can declare which adapter a FUTURE slice will use.

default_entity_id.description: An OPTIONAL hint at which canonical BAGMAN entity evidence from this mailbox will usually belong to — a DEFAULT/SUGGESTION only, exactly like `core.source.Source.governed_entity_hint`. Never an ownership assertion: evidence observed from this mailbox does not automatically become this entity's, and this field is never treated as a canonical invariant (`mailbox == company` must never be encoded anywhere as true). Validated (when non-null) against the real canonical entity registry at creation/update time by the HTTP layer (`app/api/routers/mailboxes.py`), mirroring `app/api/routers/xero.py::_require_entity`'s own pattern — this component does not import `core.entity`/`EntityRepository` directly to keep that validation at the same orchestration layer Xero's own does it at, rather than duplicating it here.

enabled.description: Convenience flag kept in lock-step with `status` by `services/mailbox/mailbox.py::transition` — `true` if and only if `status == "ACTIVE"`. Exists so a GUI/consumer can render enabled/disabled at a glance without decoding `status` itself.

status.description: This mailbox definition's own closed lifecycle (see `services/mailbox/mailbox.py::ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS` for the full, documented transition table). `ACTIVE`/`DISABLED` are both non-destructive, freely reversible sub-states of 'still a live definition'; `RETIRED` is the GUI's 'Delete/Remove' action's real effect — the row is PRESERVED (never physically removed) so any future evidence provenance referencing this mailbox is never orphaned. `RETIRED` is terminal in this slice (a documented judgment call, see that module's own docstring) — there is no transition back out of it; a mistakenly-retired mailbox is corrected by creating a fresh definition, not by reviving the old row's history.

connection_state.description: Honest, non-secret connection/readiness status — NEVER faked. Every mailbox created in THIS slice is `NOT_CONFIGURED` and STAYS `NOT_CONFIGURED` for its entire lifetime here: no code path anywhere in this slice can ever set this field to anything else, `CONNECTED` above all (nothing actually connects to any provider yet — see `services/mailbox/mailbox.py`'s own module docstring). `AUTH_REQUIRED`/`READY_FOR_CONNECTION` are forward-declared vocabulary for a FUTURE slice's real adapter/OAuth work (mirrors `services.needs_you.needs_you.ITEM_TYPE_XERO_ACCOUNT_REQUIRED`'s own 'declared now, no producer yet' pattern) — not reachable today.

last_connection_check_at.description: UTC timestamp of the most recent live connection/readiness check. Always `null` in this slice — no such check exists yet.

last_successful_sweep_at.description: UTC timestamp of the most recent successful mail sweep. Always `null` in this slice — no sweep/fetch capability exists yet anywhere behind this contract.

last_error_code.description: Short, safe, non-secret error code from the most recent connection attempt. Always `null` in this slice.

last_error_detail.description: Short, safe, NON-SECRET description of the most recent connection error — never a raw token/header/provider response body. Always `null` in this slice.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp this mailbox definition was first created.

updated_at.description: UTC timestamp of the most recent change to this row (any field, not only `status`).

metadata.description: Free-form, NON-SECRET display/context data only. Never a password/token/secret of any kind — see this schema's own top-level description.
